record.paper_title: Open problems on graph eigenvalues studied with AutoGraphiX
record.original_question: For every tricyclic graph G on n vertices with n = 20 or n >= 22, is the energy E(G) at most E(P_n^{6,6;6}), where P_n^{6,6;6} is the graph formed from three copies of C_6 and a path P_(n-18) by joining two of the 6-cycles to one endpoint of the path and the third 6-cycle to the other endpoint, one edge per attachment? Must equality occur only for G isomorphic to P_n^{6,6;6}?

evidence.quote: The problem of finding the tricyclic graphs maximizing the energy remains open.
Conjecture 5.11 Let G be a tricyclic graph on n vertices with n = 20 or n >= 22. Then E(G) <= E(P6,6;6_n) with equality if and only if G ≡ P6,6;6_n.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a finite simple graph $G$, let $\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\dots,\lambda_n$ be the eigenvalues of its adjacency matrix, and define the graph energy by
$$E(G)=\sum_{i=1}^n |\lambda_i|.$$
A connected graph on $n$ vertices is called tricyclic if it has exactly $n+2$ edges. For integers $n\ge 19$, let $P_n^{6,6;6}$ denote the tricyclic graph constructed as follows: take three vertex-disjoint copies of the $6$-cycle $C_6$ and a path $P_{n-18}$ on $n-18$ vertices; attach two of the $6$-cycles to one endpoint of the path by adding one edge from each cycle to that endpoint, and attach the third $6$-cycle to the other endpoint of the path by adding one edge.

Prove or disprove: for every tricyclic graph $G$ on $n$ vertices with $n=20$ or $n\ge 22$,
$$E(G)\le E(P_n^{6,6;6}),$$
with equality if and only if $G\cong P_n^{6,6;6}$.
artifact.status_search_result: Searches indicate that while analogous conjectures for unicyclic and bipartite bicyclic graphs have been completely resolved (Huo–Li–Shi and collaborators), the tricyclic case remains open: partial results restrict the conjecture to bipartite tricyclic graphs with three vertex-disjoint cycles and verify it apart from a small number of subclasses, but no complete proof has been reported.

status_evidence.title: On a Conjecture about Tricyclic Graphs with Maximal Energy
status_evidence.snippet: Partial progress proves the conjecture for bipartite tricyclic graphs with three vertex-disjoint cycles apart from several subclasses.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture has been verified only partially; the tricyclic maximum-energy problem remains open in general.

status_evidence.title: Complete solution to a conjecture on the maximal energy of unicyclic graphs
status_evidence.snippet: The analogous unicyclic conjecture has been completely resolved using Coulson integral formula techniques.
status_evidence.claim: Related lower-cycle-rank conjectures are solved, but the tricyclic analogue is still listed as open.
